title: Mitigate CPU-side jitter with prioritized token buckets and scatter-gather DMA batching
creator: Luca Moreno
description: Background: We observe intermittent CPU-side jitter during high-concurrency prefill/decode workloads. The root causes are a combination of small, frequent memcpy operations between host staging buffers and GPU, contention in the general-purpose threadpool that handles prefill batching and kernel launches, and non-deterministic ordering of KV-cache priming which triggers suboptimal kernel selection. This ticket proposes a coordinated mitigation: a prioritized token-bucket scheduler on request handling threads plus a scatter-gather DMA batching layer that coalesces small memcpy ops into larger GPU DMA transactions. Goal: Reduce host-side tail latency and variance for 95th/99th percentiles without regressing median latency or throughput across mixed workloads.
implementation_steps: 1) Instrument current host memcpy sizes and frequency (microbenchmarks + prod trace sampling). 2) Implement an in-process token-bucket limiter per route with priority classes (real-time, interactive, background). 3) Add a scatter-gather DMA queue that groups contiguous staging buffers into a single pinned-memory DMA submission. 4) Replace ad-hoc memcpy paths with DMA queue producer/consumer; keep zero-copy fallback for unsupported hardware. 5) Introduce a dedicated small threadpool for async DMA completions and kernel-launch bookkeeping to avoid starving general-purpose pool. 6) Add heuristics in kernel-selector to prefer kernels optimized for contiguous KV-cache layout when DMA coalescing is active. 7) Run canary against runtime-1.24 with synthetic and customer-like traces, measure P50/P95/P99 and CPU utilization. 8) Roll out via canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global with automated rollback on quality/regression alerts.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Tradeoffs: Coalescing increases latency for the first token of a small request due to batching window; mitigated by priority token-buckets that bypass coalescing for high-priority requests. Using a dedicated threadpool reduces contention but increases overall thread count and pinning complexity (NUMA awareness required). Kernel-selection tie-in: prefer contiguous-optimized kernels when DMA batch sizes exceed threshold; risk of oscillation if kernel metrics used in feedback loop. Decision: start with conservative batch windows (max 1.5ms or 128KB), enable NUMA-affinity for DMA worker threads, and instrument feedback before aggressive optimizer changes.
acceptance_criteria: - P95 tail latency for chat/prefill workloads reduced by >=20% on representative clusters vs baseline. - P99 tail latency reduced by >=10% without >3% regression in median latency. - CPU host utilization reduction in the prefill pipeline by >=15% during 90th-percentile load. - No increase in token failure rate or decoding correctness regressions. - All changes covered by unit and integration tests; load-test dashboard updated and linked.
progress_updates: 2026-03-12: Spike completed; identified memcpy hotspots in host-staging (attached flamegraphs). 2026-03-13: Prototype token-bucket scheduler merged to feature branch (ENG-84621-scheduler-proto) and running against internal loadgen. 2026-03-14: DMA scatter-gather queue initial PR opened for internal review; synthetic runs show 18% P95 improvement but +0.8% median. Observed kernel-selection mismatch for KV-cache priming; added kernel-selector flag to opt-in for contiguous kernels.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket behavior and priority classes. Integration test that runs multi-tenant loadgen with/without DMA coalescing and verifies latency and correctness. Long-running soak test (24h) on canary cluster with realistic customer traces. Add e2e test that measures kernel-selector choices under varying batch sizes.
risk_mitigation: Fallback path: maintain existing memcpy path behind a feature flag for quick rollback. Conservative default batch window and size limits. Monitor rollout with automated alerts tied to latency SLOs and model-output quality checks. Coordinate with SRE for kernel-driver upgrades if DMA path requires newer drivers.
notes: Review feedback from PM/Perf: confirm memory pinning cost across instance types; design doc updated with NUMA guidelines. Next steps: finish DMA worker NUMA-affinity, add telemetry for kernel-selection, and schedule perf review with Research/Applied ML to validate no quality regressions.
